text: Oommen Chandy (31 October 1943 – 18 July 2023) was an Indian lawyer and statesman who served as the 10th chief minister of Kerala from 2004 to 2006 and from 2011 to 2016. He also served as the leader of the opposition in the Kerala Legislative Assembly from 2006 to 2011. Born on 31 October 1943 in Kumarakom, Kottayam district, as the son of Baby and K. O. Chandy of Karottu Vallakkalil house, he was named after his paternal grandfather, V. J. Oommen, a member of the Travancore Legislative Council. He began his political career as an activist in the Kerala Students Union (KSU), the student wing of the Indian National Congress, serving as unit president at St. George High School, Puthupally, and later becoming state president. He completed his pre-university course at CMS College, Kottayam, earned a B.A. in economics from St. Berchmans College, Changanassery, and obtained a bachelor's degree in law (LL.B) from the Government Law College, Ernakulam. He served as president of the State Youth Congress in 1970 and represented the Puthuppally constituency in the Kerala Legislative Assembly from 1970 until his death in 2023, making him the longest-serving member of the Kerala Legislature Assembly. He was elected to the Assembly in 1970, 1977, 1980, 1982, 1987, 1991, 1996, 2001, 2006, 2011, 2016, and 2021. During his legislative career, he served as chairman of the Public Accounts Committee from 1996 to 1998. Oommen Chandy held ministerial positions on four occasions: as minister for Labour from 11 April 1977 to 25 April 1977 in the first K. Karunakaran ministry and until 27 October 1978 in the first A. K. Antony ministry; as home minister from 28 December 1981 to 17 March 1982 in the second K. Karunakaran ministry; and as finance minister in the fourth K. Karunakaran ministry from 2 July 1991 until his resignation on 22 June 1994. In May 2004, the Indian National Congress lost all seats in Kerala, leading to the resignation of Chief Minister A. K. Antony. On 30 August 2004, Oommen was elected as Congress Legislature Party leader with approval from AICC observers and Sonia Gandhi. The Congress-led alliance retained 42 out of 140 seats and increased its vote share by nearly 10% after the general election. He resigned as chief minister on 12 May 2006 following the party's defeat in the 2006 Assembly Elections. In the 2011 assembly election, the UDF, led by Oommen Chandy, won 72 seats against the LDF's 68, securing a slender majority. He took oath on 18 May 2011 with six ministers and later added thirteen more. Under his leadership, the UDF won 16 out of 20 Lok Sabha constituencies in Kerala in 2009 and gained an upper hand in local body elections. After the 2011 victory, Congress's legislative party unanimously elected him as its leader. In 2013, Oommen Chandy received the United Nations Public Service Award for the Asia-Pacific region for "Preventing and Combating Corruption in the Public Service," presented on 27 June 2013 in Manama, Bahrain, by UN Under-Secretary-General Wu Hongbo, under the theme "Transformative e-Government and Innovation: Creating a Better Future for All." He also received recognition for his Mass Contact Programme (Jana Samparkka Paripadi) for hearing and resolving citizen complaints. His first ministry (2004–2006) adopted the motto Athivegam Bahudooram (Fast and far) and introduced measures such as unemployment allowance and welfare for labourers. He attended the 35th World Economic Forum in Davos in 2006. In 2011–2012, the Karunya benevolent scheme was implemented, providing free treatment for patients with cancer, haemophilia, kidney, and heart diseases. Forty-three Cochlear implant surgeries were conducted under a scheme for hearing-impaired children, and more organ implantation surgeries were carried out through the Mruthasanjeevani project. In 2005, Information Technology was made a compulsory subject for school-level students, making Kerala the first Indian state to do so. Victers TV, India's first public edutainment channel on EDUSAT, was inaugurated on 28 July 2005 by A. P. J. Abdul Kalam in Thiruvananthapuram. The Hill highway project, first proposed in 1960, was approved in 2005, with Oommen inaugurating its first phase between Kasaragod and Palakkad in Payyavoor on 17 January 2005. The Second Oommen ministry (2011–2016) adopted the motto Vikasanavum Karuthalum (Development and Care). It initiated several major infrastructure and welfare projects, including the Kannur International Airport, Kochi Metro, Vizhinjam International Seaport, and the Smart City project. Thiruvananthapuram and Kozhikode Light Metro projects were approved in 2012, and a suburban rail project was launched in 2013. The Technopark at Thiruvananthapuram became India's largest IT park with the inauguration of its third phase in 2014. The Taurus Downtown at Technopark was commenced between 2011 and 2016, the second phase of InfoPark, Kochi was inaugurated in May 2015, and Phase two of InfoPark Thrissur was completed during the same period. The Park Centre of Cybercity at Kozhikode was opened on 15 February 2014 by IT Minister P.K. Kunhalikutty, and UL Cyberpark at Kozhikode was inaugurated in January 2016. During his tenure, 12 new Taluks, 28 new Municipalities, and the Kannur Municipal Corporation were formed, marking the largest Taluk delimitation in Kerala since 1957. State highways were constructed, and the decision to widen national highways to 45 metres (148 ft) was made in 2014. A total of 227 road bridges costing nearly Rs 1,600 crore were built, the most in the state's history. The Kozhikode bypass was completed, and works on Kollam and Alappuzha bypasses were restarted. The Karamana-Kaliyikkavila and Kazhakootam-Karode bypasses for Thiruvananthapuram were initiated. The Kochi-Mangalore GAIL pipeline was commissioned in 2013. Oommen Chandy's administration ensured at least one government medical college in each of Kerala's 14 districts, establishing new colleges starting in 2013 after a 31-year gap. The National University of Advanced Legal Studies was founded in 2005, the Indian Institute of Technology in Palakkad in 2015, Thunchath Ezhuthachan Malayalam University in Tirur in 2012, and APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University in Thiruvananthapuram in 2014. The K. R. Narayanan National Institute of Visual Science and Arts was inaugurated in January 2016. In 2015, Cochin International Airport became the world's first fully solar-powered airport with a dedicated solar plant and won the Champion of the Earth award in 2018 and the Best Airport in Asia-Pacific in 2020. The Kerala Urban Road Transport Corporation (KURTC) was formed in 2015 under KSRTC and inaugurated on 12 April 2015 at Thevara. Works on the last phase of Kollam Bypass began on 27 May 2015. Social welfare pensions were doubled during his second ministry, rising to Rs 600, with distributions ranging from Rs 800 to Rs 1,500. Pensions for the disabled and widows were increased to Rs 800, old-age pensions to Rs 1,500 for those above 75 and Rs 1,100 for those above 80. Free rations were provided to unemployed individuals, and 4,14,552 houses were distributed to homeless people. Free rice was given to those below the poverty line, and food kits were distributed during Onam, Ramadan, and Christmas. A rubber subsidy ensuring a minimum price of Rs 150/kg was introduced in 2015. The Kerala Public Service Commission appointed 1,67,096 job candidates and created 46,223 posts between 2011 and 2016, setting a record. The government prohibited liqueur in the state by discouraging bars, and political killings remained low at eleven during 2011–2016. Kerala was declared the first complete digital state of India on 27 February 2016. Twenty-six sectors were highlighted at the Emerging Kerala summit in Kochi in 2012, organized by KSIDC, with Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh inaugurating the event. Goals included 45 project proposals with over Rs 40,000 crore investment, including Bharat Petroleum's Kochi Refinery expansion (Rs 18,000 crore), Volkswagen’s engine assembly unit (Rs 2,000 crore), a hospital and pre-cast concrete unit (Rs 570 crore), and a solar energy plant (Rs 500 crore). Key projects developed post-summit included the Kochi-Mangalore GAIL pipeline, Vizhinjam International Seaport, Kochi Metro, Thiruvananthapuram and Kozhikode Light Metro, Petroleum Chemicals & Petrochemical Investment Region, Kochi-Palakkad National Investment and Manufacturing Zone, Indian Institute of Information Technology, Kottayam, Thiruvananthapuram–Kasargode Semi High Speed Rail Corridor, Kerala Seaplane, Electronic Hub at Kochi, Titanium Sponge Plant at Kollam, Oceanarium at Kochi, Bio 360 Life Sciences Park at Thiruvananthapuram, a gas-based powerplant at Cheemeni, Kasaragod, and Kochi LNG Terminal. The 2013 Kerala solar panel scam was a major scandal raised by the LDF-led opposition during the 2016 Assembly elections. In 2018, the Crime Branch found no evidence against Oommen Chandy, and the state home secretary T. K. Jose forwarded a report to the central government stating that no evidence could be collected and that the incident in the complaint did not actually occur. The case was handed over to a central agency after repeated failures by Kerala Police to prove allegations. The opposition accused corruption in the Vizhinjam International Seaport project ahead of the 2016 election. The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) identified irregularities in the Vizhinjam seaport project agreement, noting a potential additional revenue of Rs 29,217 crore for the concessionaire due to a ten-year PPP concession beyond the standard thirty-year term, based on Ernst and Young feasibility reports. In May 2017, the First Vijayan ministry appointed a three-member judicial commission under Justice C. N. Ramachandran to investigate. The commission concluded in 2018 that there was no corruption or misuse of political power in the project, stating that no specific corruption charges were made against any individual and that no evidence was presented. Justice C. N. Ramachandran emphasized that "when there is no allegation of corruption against anyone, there is no need to investigate corruption against anyone," and thus the commission found no corruption. The Pattoor Land Case was used by the LDF-led opposition ahead of the 2016 Assembly election. In February 2018, the Kerala High Court addressed the case.

The Hinjam Seaport project could generate an additional revenue of Rs 29,217 crore for the concessionaire, as projected in the Feasibility Report prepared by Ernst and Young. In May 2017, the first Vijayan ministry appointed a three-member judicial commission under Justice C. N. Ramachandran to investigate the project. The commission, which concluded in 2018, found no corruption and no misuse of political power, stating there was no evidence of corruption and that no individual faced specific allegations. Justice Ramachandran emphasized that since no one came forward with corruption charges or evidence, there was no need to investigate corruption. The Pattoor Land Case was used by the LDF-led opposition before the 2016 Kerala Legislative Assembly election. In February 2018, the Kerala High Court ruled that the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) had registered a first information report based on a wrong report prepared by Jacob Thomas, noting that the claim the property vests with Kerala Water Authority lacked any supporting document. The court rejected the case, declaring that neither Oommen nor the UDF government was involved in corruption. The Palmolein Oil Import Scam (1991–1992) involved alleged irregularities in palmolein imports by the K. Karunakaran-led UDF government through Power and Energy Limited. The LDF-led opposition accused the government in 1992, but a 2011 VACB probe found that Oommen Chandy, who was finance minister from 1991 to 1996, had no role in the corruption, as the report stated he was unaware of the decision to import palmolein via a Singapore-based firm. Oommen Chandy was diagnosed with throat cancer and began immunotherapy treatment at HCG Cancer Centre in Bengaluru in December 2022. He also underwent a laser biopsy in Germany, a procedure that reduces tumor size but does not eliminate cancer. Despite treatment, Chandy died on 18 July 2023 at the age of 79 due to complications from throat cancer at Chinmaya Mission Hospital in Bengaluru. Following his death, his body was transported to Thiruvananthapuram by chartered flight for public homage, first at the Durbar Hall and then at the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) office. The Government of Kerala declared a public holiday on 18 July 2023 and observed a two-day state mourning. A solemn funeral procession began on 19 July 2023, covering a 150 km distance from the state capital to Chandy's hometown, Puthuppally in Kottayam district; the journey, normally taking five hours, was extended to about 30 hours due to widespread public grief, with thousands lining the route. The final rites were conducted on 20 July 2023 at St. George Orthodox Church, Puthuppally, presided over by Mar Baselios Marthoma Mathews III. As an honour for his public service, Chandy was buried in a specially constructed tomb within the exclusive burial ground for Orthodox Church clergy. Respecting his wishes, the family declined state honours, with his son stating his father desired a simple funeral. After Chandy's death, his son, Chandy Oommen, contested and won the by-election. KPCC President K Sudhakaran stated that the Vizhinjam port should be named after Oommen Chandy because the port became a reality only due to his efforts.
